sample.title: Why Condos Are Getting Harder To Buy
sample.description:
Buying a condo may be about to become significantly more difficult, even for buyers with good financial standing. Beginning August 3rd, Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac are making big changes to how condominium mortgages are reviewed. Streamlined review process that applied to many transactions will now be retired. Instead, lenders will now have to conduct a more comprehensive review of a the building before the mortgage can go to Fannie Mae or Freddie Mac.

sample.title: Three days of Ukrainian strikes at 'Russian Amazon' Wildberries sites. #BBCNews
Military analysis of Ukraine's continued strikes on Russian warehouses | BBC News
sample.description:
Two Wildberries warehouses were hit by Ukrainian strikes overnight on Monday, with another site apparently linked to Russia's largest online retailer also damaged near Moscow.
 
Ukraine has been targeting facilities operated by the company - often dubbed the "Russian Amazon" - in recent weeks.
 
At least five people were killed and 10 more injured at an industrial site about 69km (43 miles) south of the Kremlin, local officials said, without confirming it was run by Wildberries.
 
Elsewhere, officials did confirm two other Wildberries sites were hit in the St Petersburg and Tver regions.
 
Kyiv says the depots supply the Russian military, which Moscow denies.

sample.title: Why 25 states sued the Trump administration over 'forced labour' tariffs | Global News Podcast
sample.description:
A group of 25 Democrat-led US states are suing President Donald Trump's administration in an effort to block his latest round of trade tariffs. 

The White House says the levies - which target 59 countries and the European Union - were imposed on nations that had not done enough to crack down on imports produced by forced labour. Among the countries affected are the UK, China, India, Canada and Mexico. 

The states' lawsuit claims that President Trump's tariffs are "arbitrary, capricious, and contrary to law", accusing the administration of using the forced labour issue as a "pretext" to replace the "Liberation Day" tariffs, which the US Supreme Court struck down in February. 

White House spokesman Kush Desai has said that the government is "using its lawful authority to obtain the elimination of unreasonable acts, policies, and practices that burden U.S. commerce". 

We speak to our North America correspondent Anthony Zurcher.

Gaza's tech workers rebuilding their lives online | BBC News
sample.description:
Ten months after the US-brokered ceasefire between Israel and Hamas, the deal has yet to deliver much of its promise: Hamas hasn’t disarmed and Israeli forces continue to bomb Gaza almost daily. Most Gazans still live in tent camps or in the rubble of half-destroyed homes.  
 
But in the most trying circumstances - some are trying to connect to the outside world and make a living with their laptops.  
 
Israel imposes tight restrictions on foreign journalists entering Gaza, so our Middle East Correspondent, Yolande Knell, has been speaking online to local tech workers.
